clue.text: One up on uncle in golf match?

definitions.text: One up on uncle in golf match?

parts.words: One up on uncle in golf match?
parts.note: uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, whose shop sign is three golden balls; one more than that names a golf format played by two pairs

explanation.surface: A golfer is one hole up on their uncle during a friendly round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' looks like a match-play score, but it means one more than the pawnbroker's sign of three balls. Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf match in which two pairs play, each player using their own ball, giving four in play at once.

clue.text: Pose with a backward author of these

definitions.text: Pose with a backward author of these

parts.words: Pose with a backward author of these
parts.note: the word pose turned backwards with a in front names the Greek storyteller, and the answer is what he wrote

explanation.surface: A slow-witted writer is asked to strike a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: A + ESOP (pose backwards) spells the Greek storyteller's name; 'these' are the moral tales he wrote, so the answer is defined through their author.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is famed for short moral tales featuring talking animals, such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Clandestine sort of delivery

definitions.meaning: a ball bowled or pitched with the hand below the shoulder

explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly or secret, and also describes a ball thrown with the arm swung below shoulder height.

clue.text: Battle, soldier, with war-god in Holy City

annotationWithheld.why: Battle, soldier, with war-god in Holy City (7) for BENARES: ARES is the war-god, but no reading of 'Battle, soldier' gives BEN; the clue looks misread in OCR and no source found it
annotationWithheld.clue: Battle, soldier, with war-god in Holy City

clue.text: Ability to change out of it in the country

indicators.note: to change the letters means rearranging them into a different word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A talent for adapting moves someone out of trouble and into this nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges ABILITY once 'out of it' has removed I and T, leaving ABILY to give the North African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African nation on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Measure's sound, it's plain

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to say the measure out loud and write what is heard

parts.note: a step is a measure, as in taking measures or a dance measure

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a measurement is reliable and obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' poses as an adjective meaning reliable and 'plain' as obvious; instead 'sound' is the homophone signal and 'plain' a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast treeless grassland of Russia and Central Asia is a kind of plain.

clue.text: Thanks to the college for the proceeds

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
King's is a famous college at Cambridge and in London

explanation.surface: A college is thanked for the money it raised.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you; King's is a Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money received by a business, its receipts or proceeds.

clue.text: Writer of 14 who inspired academics

definitions.meaning: 14 down is the title of his most famous dialogue on the ideal state
he founded the Academy in Athens, from which the word academic derives

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher wrote the Republic and founded the Academy, the namesake of all academic institutions.

clue.text: Lengthened first part of 5's centre

definitions.meaning: the middle letters of 5 across are EP, the abbreviation for a record format whose first word is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The centre of STEPPE (5 across) is EP, a record label abbreviation for 'extended play'; the first part of that phrase is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened means drawn out or prolonged, and a longer-playing record format was named the same way.

clue.text: Failing (by two) to make two hearts, the supporting call

indicators.note: falling short by two letters means two letters are dropped from what is built
two signals the word is written out twice

parts.note: taken in the singular, a heart

explanation.surface: A bridge player falls two tricks short of a contract of two hearts, and partner offers support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles HEART and 'Failing (by two)' drops its two Ts, giving the cry of approval heard in Parliament. Hearts is a bridge suit, which drives the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament members shout this to show agreement with a speaker, a call of support.

clue.text: Food served to traveller after the rest

definitions.text: Food served to traveller after the rest

parts.words: Food served to traveller after the rest
parts.note: a guesthouse offers a night's rest (a bed) and then the morning meal to the passing traveller

explanation.surface: A meal is brought to a weary traveller once everyone else has eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' seems to mean the other diners; it is a night's sleep, and the food after it is the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight lodging plus the morning meal is what a guesthouse sells to someone on the road.

clue.text: Part of one of the five towns in ancient Italy

definitions.text: Part of one of the five towns
definitions.meaning: Arnold Bennett's Five Towns are the Potteries, now Stoke-on-Trent, and Wedgwood's works district there bears this name
the land of the Etruscans in ancient central Italy

explanation.walkthrough: The Five Towns are Arnold Bennett's fictional name for the Staffordshire pottery towns of Stoke-on-Trent; Josiah Wedgwood named his factory district after the Etruscan homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name covers Wedgwood's district of Stoke and the Etruscan region of pre-Roman Italy.

clue.text: Overtaken in chase when exhausted

definitions.meaning: a quarry caught after pursuit has been caught up with
worn out, tired and in poor condition

explanation.surface: A fugitive is caught by pursuers once they are too tired to keep running.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunted prey that is caught has been chased to ground; a weary, worn-out person is likewise described with this phrase.

clue.text: Talk about us going to the lake

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about
taken as written
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Someone suggests discussing a trip the group might take to the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (circa) + US + ERIE gives the French-derived word for an informal chat or essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A causerie is an informal conversation or chatty essay, from French causer, to chat.

clue.text: State of something left outside inn

indicators.note: outside places the first word around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a relic is something left over from the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: Something is reported about a thing someone abandoned outside an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare; it is the noun, a nation. 'Something left' is a leftover from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a nation governed without a monarch, a kind of state.

clue.text: Hundreds put together this kind of horse

definitions.meaning: a hundred was an old English subdivision of a county, so a county is many of them combined
a large, heavy British draught breed

explanation.surface: Hundreds of animals combined make up this breed of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred was an old administrative division of an English county; a county was built from several of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An English county was made up of hundreds; the same word names the heavy draught breed.

clue.text: Not fair, putting out Winston in 45?

parts.note: taken as written
Clement Attlee ousted Winston Churchill as Prime Minister in the 1945 election

explanation.surface: Someone protests that the 1945 election that ousted Churchill was unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1945 general election Clement Attlee's Labour party removed Winston Churchill as Prime Minister; '45' dates that event. 'fair' reads as just, but it describes weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that is not fair is stormy or harsh, which is the usual sense of the word.

clue.text: Beginning to mark time, nonetheless, with shoe

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter
read as none-less, it drops the round letter that stands for nothing

parts.note: an occasion is a time when something happens

explanation.surface: Starting to keep time despite everything, wearing a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as 'none less': remove O (nought) from OCCASION. 'Beginning to' gives M from mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather slipper of North American origin, a type of shoe.

clue.text: Stranger could turn to 'Communist Party

indicators.note: turning these words round means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: An outsider might switch allegiance to the Communist Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could turn to' reverses RED + DO (REDDO) to give the comparative of odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger, as a comparative adjective, means more odd or peculiar.

clue.text: Some are in seconds or, minutes

definitions.meaning: athletic bests are timed in seconds

explanation.definitionFit: Sprint bests are measured in seconds, and the written account of a meeting is its official notes.

clue.text: Average amount cut from this sort of speech

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
to lance is to cut, as with a boil

explanation.surface: A typical length is trimmed from this style of address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut from' suggests something is removed; instead the cut simply follows the average, and 'from this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of speaking or idiom, as in legal parlance.

clue.text: True, sea caused such severe damage

indicators.note: damage wrecks the words, so their letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A storm at sea really did cause terrible harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' works on TRUE and SEA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern, strict and plain, close in sense to severe.

clue.text: Caller of tune holding pound for piper, perhaps

indicators.note: holding means one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: the proverb says he who pays the piper calls the tune
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The person paying for the music keeps a pound back from the piper.
explanation.walkthrough: From the proverb 'he who pays the piper calls the tune'.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper is one example of a musician who performs on an instrument.

clue.text: Sort of pipe tobacco — RN blend, not TA

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters of the named words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the Royal Navy abbreviation
taken as written, the Territorial Army abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pipe tobacco advertised as a Navy blend rather than an Army one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' mixes TOBACCO and RN, and 'not TA' removes T and A from the pool, leaving the letters of the pipe. RN is the Royal Navy, TA the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe whose bowl is made from a dried maize cob is a well-known type of tobacco pipe.

clue.text: Quartet owing rent?

annotationWithheld.why: Quartet owing rent? (5) for RIVED: IV (quartet) inside RED, but the only container signal is 'owing' (in the red), which would also have to supply RED, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Dickens in good health, said this biographer

indicators.note: said tells us the joined words are spoken aloud to give the spelling

parts.note: Boz was the pen name of Charles Dickens, and well means in good health

explanation.surface: A remark that the novelist Dickens is feeling fine, from this writer of lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Boz was Charles Dickens's early pen name; BOZ + WELL spoken aloud gives the name of Samuel Johnson's biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson, the model of English biography.

clue.text: Being intoxicated, result of this?

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk and unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being drunk comes from this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intoxicated' rearranges BEING; the whole clue describes a bout of heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking spree leaves one drunk, so drunkenness is what it produces.

clue.text: Destruction for germ in every dose?

definitions.text: Destruction for germ in every dose?

indicators.note: destruction wrecks the following words, so their letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A medicine that destroys bacteria with each dose taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destruction' scrambles GERM IN EVERY DOSE; the whole clue also describes a cure-all that kills germs every time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign remedy is a supremely effective cure, which a germ-killing dose would be.

clue.text: He doesn't invest himself, but hides nothing from others

definitions.text: He doesn't invest himself, but hides nothing from others

parts.words: He doesn't invest himself, but hides nothing from others
parts.note: invest is read in its old sense of clothe, so this person wears no clothes and conceals nothing

explanation.surface: A cautious man who never puts his own money in, yet is completely open with everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' reads as putting money in, but its older sense is to clothe; someone who wears nothing hides nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes without clothes, keeping no part of the body concealed.

clue.text: What's wrong with gold for turncoat?

parts.note: a defect is a fault, what is wrong with something
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is wrong with swapping gold for a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat abandons their side for the enemy, exactly what one who deserts does.
